BiblicalUsage: Beth-Maachah means house of pressure, and it is named twice, both times around the siege of Abel. In 2 Samuel 20:14 Sheba's flight takes him through to Abel and to Beth-maachah, and in 2 Samuel 20:15 Joab's army besieges him in Abel of Beth-maachah, casting up a bank against the city. A northern town, caught in a rebellion it did not start.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Beth-maachah's name fits the siege: pressure, from outside and from within, until a wise woman talked the city out of it.
